newsitem.title: FRANCE: French government presents key 1997 budget.
newsitem.headline: French government presents key 1997 budget.

text.p: The French government was due on Wednesday to approve a budget for 1997 which will cut taxes and spending and reduce the public deficit to ensure France meets Maastricht treaty standards on European monetary union.

French newspapers said the government would announce plans to reduce the total public deficit to 2.9 percent of gross domestic product (GDP) -- below the Maastricht limit of three percent -- from a forecast four percent this year.

While some of the reduction will come from spending cuts, economists expect the government to use a large measure of creative accounting to get the deficit down in 1997 -- the key year for deciding which countries qualify for monetary union.
Newspapers said the central government budget deficit would be reduced to 283.6 billion francs, after allowing for income tax cuts of 25 billion francs, from 288 billion this year.
The separately run social security system was expected to show a deficit of 35 billion francs next year, they said.
Excise duties on alcohol and tobacco are due to be raised to help fund the welfare system, which is expected to show a deficit of 50 billion francs this year.
Government officials declined all comment on the budget ahead of its approval.

But German Finance Minister Theo Waigel said on Tuesday that both France and Germany aimed to reduce their deficits to below three percent next year, fuelling speculation the French government would announce a 2.9 percent target.
